title: How a scene is written
blurb: This demo chapter shows every helper in the kit once. Copy its pattern; do not ship it.

scenes.heading: A question goes in, an answer comes out
scenes.caption: Three boxes, two arrows, one answer. Every word on this screen lives in the content file, not in the scene code.
scenes.question: Tom has 12 apples. He gives away 5, then buys 3. How many does he have?

scenes.heading: Two bars and a tag
scenes.caption: Bars grow while their numbers count up. The green tag says this one was tested.

scenes.heading: The five-part map
scenes.caption: The same map appears in every chapter, so you always know where you are in the machine.

scenes.heading: Letters, vectors, curves and notes
caption: First, text is cut into letters. Each letter gets its own little box.
Then each letter is turned into a row of numbers (a vector). The shading is only a picture of the numbers.
A second row of numbers is built on top of the first. A note card says what to be careful about.
scenes.note: Careful: this shading is an illustration, not real model numbers.
